standard_prerequisites.name: Tensor products commute with directed colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the end of the counted proof (lines 47757-47759)
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the finitely many polynomial data be moved down to a single stage of the colimit.

core_obligations: Choose finitely many generators x_1, ..., x_m of C_0 over B_0 and, using finiteness after base change, monic polynomials P_j over the base-changed algebra with P_j(1 tensor x_j) = 0 (proof lines 47753-47755).

Because the tensor product commutes with the directed colimit, the finitely many polynomials come from some stage i, and then P_{j,i}(1 tensor x_j) vanishes at that stage after possibly increasing i (proof lines 47756-47759).
Conclude that at that stage the base-changed map is finite (proof lines 47759-47760).
proof_roadmap: Extract finite data witnessing finiteness after the colimit (proof lines 47752-47755).
Descend the finite data to one stage using commutation of tensor products with colimits (proof lines 47756-47761).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if a base-changed map of algebras is finite and the source algebra is of finite type relative to the base, then finiteness already holds after base change along some single stage of the colimit (statement lines 47738-47750). The proof does not use a general limit-of-finite-presentation argument: it extracts the finite data witnessing finiteness, namely finitely many generators and monic polynomials, uses that tensor products commute with directed colimits to move that finite data down to one stage, and then notes that the relations still vanish there after increasing the stage (proof lines 47752-47761). The reduction of the conclusion to finitely many polynomial relations, so that descent to a stage becomes possible, is the content. H2.
